title: How indicators guide decisions
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:15Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank points either define what an indicator is or cover only how government responds to one indicator, and neither teaches how the Reserve Bank, businesses and households use indicators to make decisions.

draft.title: How indicators guide decisions
card: Economic indicators are figures such as GDP growth, unemployment and inflation. Different groups watch them to help decide what to do.
may change its budget when indicators change. For example, it may spend more on projects if unemployment is rising.
Australia's central bank, which sets the cash rate. It may raise the rate if inflation is above its target, to slow spending and price rises.
Firms use indicators to decide on hiring and investment. Households use them to decide on spending, saving and borrowing.
draft.remember: Each group reads the indicators that matter to its own choices.

a.q: Inflation in Australia is well above the Reserve Bank's target. What might the Reserve Bank do?
opts: Raise the cash rate to slow price rises
Cut the cash rate to speed up spending
Hire more workers for public projects
Raise the budget spending on roads
a.why: A higher cash rate makes borrowing dearer, which slows spending and eases price rises. Cutting the rate would push spending up, which is the wrong way when inflation is high.
a.clue: Which way should spending move to slow price rises?

b.q: Priya owns a bakery in Ballarat. Local unemployment is rising and GDP growth is slowing. Which decision best fits these indicators?
opts: Delay buying a second oven until conditions improve
Hire three more bakers to meet rising demand
Open two more shops straight away
Raise spending on new equipment this month
b.why: Weak growth and rising unemployment suggest households may spend less, so waiting to invest is sensible. The other choices expect stronger demand than the indicators show.
b.clue: Would shoppers be spending more or less in these conditions?

a.best: Raise the cash rate to slow price rises

b.best: Delay buying a second oven until conditions improve
